title: Aerobic Composting or Bio-digestion
explanation: Food residuals, fruit rinds, vegetable clippings, and tea grounds possess high moisture and organic nitrogen, making them ideal feedstock for microbial decomposition into nutrient-rich humus.
cautions: Exclude treated meats, large bones, dog/cat feces, and synthetic cooking grease from home compost bins to avoid anaerobic odors and vermin attraction.
prepSteps: Chop fibrous rinds into 1-2 inch chunks for faster decomposition.
Pair 1 part food scraps (greens) with 2 parts dry leaves or shredded brown cardboard (browns).
Aerate the pile weekly to maintain aerobic aerobic microbes.

title: Rigid Polymer Segregation (PET #1 / HDPE #2 / PP #5)
explanation: Clean rigid plastics are shredded, melted, and pelletized into secondary raw resin, displacing virgin petrochemical extraction.
cautions: Soft plastic bags, cling wraps, and contaminated greasy food containers jam optical sorting belts and degrade recycled polymer batches.
prepSteps: Empty completely and rinse out leftover liquids or oils.
Check resin identification code (#1, #2, #5 are widely accepted; #3, #6, #7 often require specialized drop-offs).
Keep bottle caps screwed on if requested by municipal MRF.

title: Dry Fiber Reclamation
explanation: Unsoiled corrugated boxes, newsprint, and paperboard can be repulped up to 5-7 times to manufacture new packaging material.
cautions: Grease, pizza cheese oils, wax linings, and plastic tape severely spoil paper repulping vats. Greasy cardboard should be torn and added to compost instead.
prepSteps: Flatten boxes to optimize bin volume and logistics efficiency.
Remove heavy packing tapes, staples, and plastic film envelopes.
Keep thoroughly dry until municipal collection.

title: Closed-Loop Smelting & Ingot Casting
explanation: Aluminum beverage cans and tin-plated steel food cans are infinitely recyclable without property degradation, saving 95% of the energy needed for virgin bauxite smelting.
cautions: Aerosol spray cans containing pressurized solvents or chemical paint cans require hazardous waste drop-off.
prepSteps: Rinse food or sweet drink residue to deter insect contamination.
Lightly crush aluminum cans to save storage space.
Do not mix with lithium battery scrap.

title: Cullet Remelt & Container Circularity
explanation: Container glass (jars and beverage bottles) melts cleanly at 1400°C into new cullet, requiring 30% less energy than raw silica sand melting.
cautions: Do not mix window panes, mirrors, ceramic mugs, Pyrex borosilicate cookware, or light bulbs with bottle glass; their different melting temperatures cause defects in new bottles.
prepSteps: Rinse thoroughly with cold water.
Remove metal or plastic caps (recycle metal lids separately).
Do not break containers before dropping off at bottle banks.

title: Garment Reuse, Downcycling or Fiber Shredding
explanation: Wearable garments should be washed and donated; frayed fabrics can be shredded into acoustic insulation, car upholstery padding, or cleaning rags.
cautions: Wet or moldy textiles cannot be stored or shredded and may cross-contaminate fabric sorting bins.
prepSteps: Launder and dry items thoroughly prior to collection.
Separate wearable clothing from damaged rags.
Remove heavy buttons or non-fabric zippers if donating to shredding stations.

title: Certified WEEE Recovery & Hazardous Isolation
explanation: Printed circuit boards, lithium batteries, cables, and appliances contain precious gold, copper, and palladium, alongside toxic lead and mercury.
cautions: NEVER place electronics or batteries into standard household waste or recycling bins. Damaged lithium cells cause severe compactor truck fires.
prepSteps: Tape battery terminals (lithium/NiMH) with electrical tape to avoid short circuits.
Perform factory reset and remove memory cards from smart devices.
Take to designated municipal e-waste collection depot or take-back kiosks.

title: Manual Material Inspection & Segregation
explanation: The item could not be categorized with sufficient confidence, or comprises non-separable composite materials (e.g. foil-lined chip packets, composite blenders).
cautions: Do not guess recyclable status; wish-cycling creates contamination penalties for waste management facilities.
prepSteps: Inspect the material layers (is there foil, plastic laminate, or mixed adhesive?).
Check manufacturer packaging disposal instructions.
If in doubt and no local take-back program exists, place in residual dry waste.
